name: Magnetometer and compass heading
plain: Reads magnetic field and heading; iOS true heading uses location services.
meaning: Reveals orientation and nearby magnetic objects (cars, metal), and is used for indoor positioning.

ios.api_surface: Magnetic heading raw; true north needs location

limits.headline: Can use your phone's compass and magnetic field, with a location link for true north
limits.user_action: Nothing, or you allow location when a compass wants true north on iPhone
can: Measure the magnetic field in microtesla
Show compass heading toward magnetic north
Give true north on iPhone after location is allowed
Help find nearby metal or detect a magnet case
cannot: Show true north on iPhone without location access
Give your location from the compass
Ask you first on Android; no prompt is used
limits.reach_label: Compass and field, while in use
limits.differs: Android needs no prompt for magnetic readings. iPhone raw heading works, but true north needs location services.

story.what_it_is: An app reads the magnetic field, which powers the compass and can show nearby metal.

marketing.name: Position sensors
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps use the magnetic field sensor for a compass and orientation.

story.for_you: You see it as a compass needle in a map or a sky app that points to the right star. Most of the time you never notice the app reading it. It can also help place you inside a building.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to turn maps to face your way, power AR and help find your spot indoors. It is a small fingerprint bit too, since each phone's compass has its own error.

use_cases.example: A map app rotates the map to point the way you face while you walk.
A star gazing app overlays constellations on the sky and follows your phone as you move it.
An AR treasure hunt points an arrow toward a hidden item.
A pilgrim or hiking app shows true north and a direction to a landmark.
A metal detector app shows spikes when the magnetic field changes near a pipe.
A tracker uses small magnetic quirks to tell phones apart, or maps indoor fields to find where you are.

story.android_note: Android apps read the magnetic field with no prompt.
story.ios_note: iPhone heading is available with no prompt, but true north needs location services.
